Hannah / team —

I've filled the spreadsheet for the telemetry/logging rows (see folder). Summary of key responses (for the Aurora highlight):

1) Request/response logs (application telemetry):
- Retention: default operational logs retained for 90 days. Customers can request extended retention for Dedicated/Private deployments; Hosted tier can export to the customer's external storage for long-term retention.
- Contents: request metadata, timestamps, request-id, model variant, per-token latency metrics, and scored quality metrics. By default we do NOT persist full prompt text beyond short-term cache windows unless customer opt-in for debugging.

2) Model telemetry & traces (runtime metrics, kernel telemetry):
- Retention: aggregated telemetry (metrics/telemetry rolls) retained 365 days; raw runtime traces (dumps) kept for 30 days unless flagged for incident root-cause.
- Evidence: we can provide a sample telemetry manifest and the metrics retention policy excerpt from our observability product.

3) KV / prefix cache and in-memory artifacts:
- Design: KV cache is ephemeral and maintained in GPU process memory; it's not written to durable storage in normal operation. Cache snapshots are only produced during customer-enabled debugging sessions and then uploaded to customer-controlled storage when requested.

4) Prompt storage and PII handling:
- By default Hosted API does not keep full prompt bodies persistently. Transient traces for routing/diagnostics include truncated hashes (not full text). Customers with Dedicated or Private deployments control their own persistence policies and can opt-in to store prompts for debugging; when stored, Redwood provides redaction tooling and can remove retained data on request.

5) Encryption and key management:
- All stored telemetry and logs at rest are encrypted with customer-segregated keys for Dedicated/Private, and with service-managed KMS keys for Hosted. KMS key rotation and access logs are available as SOC 2 exhibits.

Attachments prepared and uploaded to the shared folder: redwood-soc2-report-2027.pdf, redwood-telemetry-dataflow.png, request-id-sample.txt (redacted).

I'll also include short control narratives mapping SIG rows II.2.x -> SOC 2 CC6 / ISO 27001 A12 equivalents.

Karthik
Principal Security Engineer
